analysis.title: Oct Employment underscores an expanding economy -- inflation will follow, the Fed will lag, and equities are repricing not collapsing
key_insights: Blitz argues the October jobs report shows an expanding economy and rejects the idea that 25,000/month payroll growth is the new normal. Last year was a non-recession recession that did not turn into a recession because of sustained fiscal expansion.

TS Lombard expects the Fed's tightening cycle to need more hikes than the Fed or markets expect. Blitz says a 50bp hike in December is possible because Republican control in DC has collapsed, but Warsh probably will not do it. Blitz calls the 50bp bet a good lottery ticket.
Blitz sees the AI corner of the equity market reverting to the mean on forward P/E. He calls this a necessary repricing that will not bring Fed support and does not put the whole market at risk.
Blitz's sequence is that hiring follows profits and inflation follows hiring. Inflation pressure takes hold in 2027 and base inflation will be higher then.

Blitz urges caution on a wage surge. US firms are adopting AI, which will cap wages and cut employment in high-wage, high-skill jobs eventually. Foreign sourcing of goods is another escape valve if a Democratic Congress reverses tariffs.

October hiring was broad-based. High-tech related industry employment rose 31,300 M/M versus 78,600 for private payrolls excluding tech and health care. Since January 2024 the tech sector has shed 128,000 jobs versus a 578,000 increase for private payrolls excluding tech and health.
Average hourly earnings rose 1.7% M/M in October after 2.2% in September. Blitz will watch whether the Atlanta Fed wage tracker gap between job leavers and stayers widens.

Total labor income (aggregate weekly payrolls index) rose 0.5% in October and 0.5% on a 3M moving average basis. Blitz expects a rebound in October retail sales ex autos and gasoline despite higher gasoline prices.

Blitz says the current equity volatility is a repricing of tech and not a forerunner of collapse. The real funds rate is 0.9% today versus 4.8% when the market topped in 2000. Bank loans are up 7.8% SAAR over 12 weeks and 6.9% Y/Y. Blitz has a zero 10-year equity return outlook and says insurance is cheap.

sector_views.rationale: Forward P/E in the AI corner is reverting to the mean. Blitz calls it a necessary repricing and not a forerunner of collapse.

macro_indicators.indicator: Private payrolls ex tech and health care

macro_indicators.interpretation: Tech hiring joined the upturn, though the sector is down 128,000 jobs since January 2024.
Follows a 2.2% rise in September. Blitz urges caution on how far wages surge.
Supports a rebound in retail sales ex autos and gasoline.
Far below the 4.8% level at the 2000 market top, so policy is not yet restrictive.
Blitz calls a 50bp hike a good lottery ticket while saying the Fed will lag.

trade_ideas.description: Bet on a 50bp Fed hike in December
trade_ideas.rationale: Blitz says the market pays you to take the outlier bet and a Warsh-led Fed with no Republican hegemony in DC can go 50 if it wants.
trade_ideas.risk: Warsh is a dove squawking like a hawk and probably will not do 50.

risk_factors: Higher wages could compress profits and equity valuations.
Inflation rises in 2027 as hiring picks up.
vol_and_positioning: Blitz says insurance is cheap and has told clients so all year.
Markets are fearful about equities, which puts a floor under fixed-income prices.
geopolitical: Collapse of Republican hegemony in DC and a Democratic Congress pushing to reverse tariffs.

tension_points.bull_case: Cheap money, a 0.9% real funds rate, bank loans up 7.8% SAAR and accelerating employment are not the conditions for an equity collapse. The AI-led drop is a mean reversion in forward P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: Hiring-led inflation in 2027 and higher wages could compress profits, and the Fed will need more hikes than expected. Blitz's 10-year equity return outlook is zero.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A real funds rate approaching the 4.8% level seen at the 2000 market top.
